children: Japanese regional utility Chubu Electric Power Co. on Monday announced that the company's two highest officials will resign next month over a data falsification scandal involving its Hamaoka nuclear power plant in Shizuoka Prefecture, central Japan.

According to Chubu Electric, Chairman Satoru Katsuno and President Kingo Hayashi will step down on Oct. 1. Minoru Yasui, who now serves as a senior managing executive officer, will succeed Hayashi as president.

Also on Monday, the regional utility released an investigative committee report regarding the manipulation of data on seismic ground motion at the Hamaoka nuclear power plant. The report revealed that the data manipulation was caused partly by the department in charge of Chubu Electric Power's nuclear division being reprimanded by the company's executive team over the slow progress of screening by the Nuclear Regulation Authority to determine if operations could be restarted at the Hamaoka plant.
